newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Aviastar shut until Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Aviastar shut until Sept 30.

text.p: Russia's AO Aviastar aircraft manufacturer which suspended operations on August 21 will remain idle until September 30 because it lacks parts and finance, a company official said on Thursday.

"Due to the serious problems of our enterprise, its management has decided that Aviastar will stay closed until September 30," Yuri Marnykh, Secretary of the board of directors, told Reuters by phone from the company's headquarters in the central Russian town of Ulyanovsk.
Marnykh said the company, which produces heavy cargo An-124 and passenger Tu-204 planes, was initially forced to stop work for the period of August 21-31.
"But the company did not manage to resolve some of its most pressing problems then," Marnykh said.
He said one of the most painful issues for Aviastar was irregular or non-existent deliveries of many components from its suppliers all over Russia, many of whom are also in difficulty.
Marnykh said the Russian government was delaying issues of guarantees for deals with Aviastar's foreign partners, and this was hurting its finances.

"Earlier this year we agreed with Egypt's Kato Aromatic company to sell it 30 cargo and passenger planes, but the deal is still up in the air, because we have got no guarantee from the government so far," he said.
Marnykh denied some media reports saying that Aviastar's debts of some 130 billion roubles to the local power company Ulyanovskenergo were the main cause of the shut-down.
"Yes, we owe money for electricity, but we and Ulyanovskenergo are now close to a mutually acceptable solution," he said.
He also denied reports of a strike of Aviastar's 28,000 workers.
"Our workers just sit at home, although earlier this week many of them, unpaid for months, took part in a one-day protest actions and blocked roads and railways," he said.
